header.title: How to Troubleshoot Humidistats
header.description: This guide provides step-by-step instructions for diagnosing and troubleshooting issues with humidistats. Learn how to identify common problems and perform basic repairs to ensure proper humidity control.

steps.description: Connect the unit to power and activate it.
actions: Plug in the unit
Switch it on

steps.description: Verify that the pilot light on the control panel is illuminated.
actions: check pilot light
go to Step 5 if pilot light is on

steps.description: Troubleshoot the appliance by checking the outlet and circuit breaker.
actions: check outlet with an outlet tester
try plugging it into a different outlet
check the circuit breaker panel for a tripped breaker
reset the breaker

steps.description: Check the unit's fuse for continuity with a multimeter and replace it if burnt out.
actions: check for power at the outlet
check for a fuse on the unit
test for continuity with a multimeter
replace the fuse if it is burnt out

steps.description: If the unit doesn't power on, adjust the humidistat and then unplug the unit if it still fails to turn on.
actions: Turn on the power
Adjust the integrated humidistat for the maximum humidity setting (for a humidifier)
Adjust the integrated humidistat for the minimum setting (for a dehumidifier)
Unplug the unit from its outlet

steps.description: This step involves accessing the float switch, testing the circuit by shorting the wires, and troubleshooting the unit's power.
actions: Get access to the float switch
Unplug both wires from their connectors
Short the two wires together to close the circuit
Plug the unit back in
If it still doesn’t come on, unplug the unit from its outlet
Leave the float switch wires together

steps.description: Remove covers from the unit to access the humidistat controller, exercising safety precautions.
actions: Remove necessary covers
Gain access to the humidistat controller
Do not troubleshoot with the unit plugged in
Wear insulated gloves while taking electrical readings

steps.description: Test the humidifier's connections for 120 VAC with a multimeter, and diagnose a defective humidistat if voltage is missing.
actions: Set multimeter to at least 120 AC volts
Plug the humidifier back in
Touch the ground probe against the grounded metal chassis
Touch the red probe on each of the two connections
Set the humidifier humidity on maximum
Set the dehumidifier on the minimum setting
Check the readings
Assume the humidistat is defective and replace it with a new one if one connection has no voltage present

steps.description: If readings are good for a humidifier, replace the fan motor; otherwise, proceed to the next step for a portable dehumidifier.
actions: check readings
replace fan motor
proceed to Step 10

steps.description: If the compressor doesn't run with voltage present, it likely indicates a faulty compressor requiring professional repair and replacement.
actions: Check for voltage at the humidistat
Observe if the compressor runs
Confirm a faulty compressor (requires certified repair shop)
Bring the compressor to a certified repair shop for confirmation and replacement

steps.description: If the compressor motor is running but the condenser isn't refrigerating, test the time-delay relay by shorting its leads to see if the compressor engages.
actions: Listen for the compressor motor running.
Observe if refrigeration is happening on the condenser.
Identify a potential refrigerant leak or defective time-delay relay.
Locate the time-delay relay.
Short the two leads of the time-delay relay with a jumper wire for a few seconds.
Listen for the compressor coming on.

steps.description: Reconnect the wires previously removed from the float switch to their terminals.
actions: Plug the two wires removed from the float switch back into their respective terminals.

steps.description: Open the water line valve by pushing down on the float.
actions: push down on the float
open the valve

steps.description: Troubleshoot water flow by checking the water line and ensuring all valves are open.
actions: check water line
ensure valves are open

steps.description: This step involves troubleshooting a humidifier injector nozzle by checking for clogs and testing the solenoid valve.
actions: Turn off the humidistat.
Verify if the injector’s nozzle tip is not plugged with some dirt or debris.
Unscrew and remove the nozzle tip.
Have someone turn the humidistat to its maximum setting briefly.
Check if water starts coming through.
Replace the spray nozzle with a new one (if water comes through).
Screw the nozzle tip back on (if no water comes through).
Check the solenoid valve.

steps.description: This step involves locating the solenoid valve, disconnecting the water line, and briefly activating the humidistat to check water flow.
actions: Follow the water line back from the spray nozzle to the solenoid valve.
Remove the water line from the injector’s side of the valve.
Have someone briefly turn the humidistat to its maximum.
Observe water flowing.

steps.description: Troubleshoot a lack of water flow by checking the solenoid valve's electrical connections and coil.
actions: Remove the cover from the solenoid
Expose the electrical connections
Turn the humidistat on maximum
Use a multimeter to check for 24 volts across the electromagnet

steps.description: Troubleshoot the humidistat by disconnecting its wires and testing for continuity with a multimeter.
actions: Open up the humidistat
Disconnect the wires going to the control board
Set multimeter on continuity
Place probes on the humidifier’s terminals
Turn the humidity level to its maximum setting

steps.description: If continuity was detected in the previous step, the control board is likely defective and needs replacement.
actions: Check for continuity
Identify defective control board
Replace control board
